solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird or creature unlikely to fly, given time

parts.note: a pig, from the saying 'pigs might fly' for something that will never happen
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a bird, or else a beast that will never get airborne however long you wait.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common bird, so the wider class names it.

clue.text: Songwriter's son adopted by fortune-teller

indicators.note: adopted by means taken into, so the son goes inside

parts.note: a palmist reads palms to tell fortunes
S abbreviates son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A songwriter's boy is taken in by a clairvoyant.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalmist composes psalms, sacred songs, so is a songwriter of a kind.

clue.text: Hardly mention what an undercoat may need

definitions.meaning: to treat a topic quickly and evasively, barely touching on it
a coat of shiny paint applied on top of a primer layer

explanation.definitionFit: To skate past a subject is one sense; read literally, a shiny finish applied on top of a base coat is the other.

clue.text: Stone cross to the south of old New York

indicators.note: in a down clue, to the south of means below, so the cross comes after

parts.note: X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A stone marker shaped like a cross lies south of old New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded semi-precious stone, a form of chalcedony.

clue.text: Shabby, but had the courage to embrace Roger undressed!

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: dared means had the courage to do something

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters of the name go

explanation.surface: A cheeky tale of someone bold enough to hug a naked Roger, which was shabby behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undressed' strips the outer letters off the name, leaving OGE; the exclamation mark plays up the naked image.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-eared pages are worn and turned down at the corners, hence tatty or shabby.

clue.text: Where one's left, for example, after being dismissed?

definitions.text: Where one's left, for example, after being dismissed?

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other

parts.note: out means dismissed, as a batter is in cricket
left is one side, as in left side

explanation.surface: Asking where you end up once you have been sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: a batter given out leaves the field and waits beyond its boundary. The parse is shown in answer order: OUT first, then SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thrown out is left beyond the door or boundary, in the open air.

clue.text: Pulling out spear-carrier shortly before film director's call

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the other
shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a spear-carrier is a walk-on actor with no lines, an extra
'Action!' is what a film director calls to start a take

explanation.surface: An extra is removed just before the director shouts to begin filming.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraction is the act of drawing something out, as a tooth is pulled by a dentist.

clue.text: Greek character, doctor, in shape

parts.note: rho is the Greek letter R
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A Greek man who is a doctor and keeps in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a four-sided geometric figure with equal sides.

clue.text: Superior light unit thrown into river

indicators.note: thrown into means put inside, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
the lux is the SI unit of illuminance

explanation.surface: A top-quality lamp has been tossed into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: De luxe means luxurious or of superior quality.

clue.text: Certain trade union's covered medical procedure

indicators.note: covered means wrapped round, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A particular union has paid for someone's operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for 'has': SURE has covered TU.
explanation.definitionFit: A suture is stitching up a wound or incision, done by a surgeon.

clue.text: Columnist shot in a city in front of relative

indicators.note: in front of means the first part comes before the next
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
NY is short for New York City
a shot is an attempt, a go
an aunt is a family relative

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer is gunned down in a city just ahead of a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like gunfire but means an attempt, as in 'have a shot'.
explanation.definitionFit: An agony aunt writes a newspaper advice column answering readers' problems, so is a kind of columnist.

clue.text: Fish beginning to rise in cost

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the other piece

parts.note: a toll is a charge or cost, as on a road or bridge

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The price of fish is starting to go up.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a moving boat; here a verb.

clue.text: Burnt residue on bottom of grim brew

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the residue follows the letter
the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: ash is what is left after burning

explanation.surface: Charred dregs at the bottom of some nasty brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is a brewing mixture of malt steeped in hot water, so a kind of brew.

clue.text: Sound producer of Cats perhaps before television

indicators.note: before puts the first part ahead of the second

parts.note: Cats is a famous stage musical, so an example of one
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: Something that makes noise, maybe cats, out ahead of the TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' looks like noisy animals but is the Lloyd Webber show.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical box plays a tune when opened, a small mechanical device that makes music.

clue.text: Female ass in pond — time for such protection

indicators.note: in places the ass inside the body of water

parts.note: a lake is a large pond
a jack, or jackass, is a male donkey

explanation.surface: A she-donkey stands in a pond: time to put on protective gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A flak jacket is armoured clothing worn as protection against shrapnel and bullets.

clue.text: South-eastern French town or city

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
ville is the French word for town

explanation.surface: Choosing between a town in south-east France and a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seville is a major city of Andalusia in southern Spain.

clue.text: Surviving Texan shot twin, dismissing victory

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are scrambled
dismissing means sending away, so letters are removed from the word

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A Texan who shot his twin brother survived, though the win was taken from him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles TEXAN to EXTAN; 'dismissing' takes WIN from TWIN, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant describes something still in existence, synonymous with surviving.

clue.text: Strange thing to try to flog — a bird

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters are made into an unusual order

parts.note: to hawk is to go about trying to sell goods

explanation.surface: An odd item to sell, a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The nighthawk is an American nightjar, a bird active at dusk.

clue.text: Result of panic in the stock market?

definitions.text: Result of panic in the stock market?

parts.words: Result of panic in the stock market?
parts.note: stock read as livestock: a herd of panicking cattle at a market rushes off

explanation.surface: A financial crash caused by panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock market' suggests shares, but read it as a livestock market.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden mass rush of frightened animals is caused by panic in a herd.

clue.text: Runs after cash-strapped agent

indicators.note: after puts the runs following the other piece

parts.note: broke means having no money
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Somebody chases a penniless agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker acts as an intermediary agent buying and selling for others.

clue.text: Tree found in socialist golf club?

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist or communist
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A tree grows at a left-wing golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: The redwood is a giant Californian conifer, a type of tree.

clue.text: December, except the middle, should be a dry spell

indicators.note: except the middle keeps only the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: ought means should, as in 'you ought to go'

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: apart from mid-month, December should be dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long period without rainfall, a dry spell.

clue.text: Blasted sailors getting in flipping late

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the sailors go inside
flipping means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: late means dead, as in 'the late king'
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Damned sailors arriving annoyingly late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns the word for late round to DAED; it looks like a mild curse in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Darned and blasted are both mild euphemistic curses meaning damned.

clue.text: How to pay for verification, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a check is a verification

explanation.surface: Asking how to pay for an identity check.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written order to a bank, a method of payment.

clue.text: Stranded on a trip with no booze!

parts.note: high means intoxicated by drugs, on a trip
and means together with
dry means without alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone left stuck on a holiday where no alcohol was served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey but is drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Left high and dry is an idiom for being abandoned without help, like a ship beached by the tide.

clue.text: Look around back of larder and eat

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: gaze means look steadily

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone scans the back of the larder and has a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: To graze is to eat small amounts often, a snacking sense from animals feeding on grass.

clue.text: Pastures temporarily holding stock

indicators.note: holding means the words contain the letters, which run across them

explanation.surface: Fields being used for a while to keep livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like farm animals but means the main stalk of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock and stem both mean the main stalk or trunk of a plant, onto which grafts are made.

clue.text: One's levy cut by half for land offshore

parts.note: I is one, so one's gives I and S

indicators.note: cut by half keeps just the first half of the word

explanation.surface: One person's tax is halved for owning land offshore.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, land surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Particle requiring question mark? Millions lost

indicators.note: lost means the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: M abbreviates million

explanation.surface: A tiny particle needs a question mark, and millions have gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A quark is a subatomic particle that makes up protons and neutrons.

clue.text: Make too much of condition after having finished first

indicators.note: after puts the condition behind the other piece, which comes first

parts.note: over means finished, at an end
state means condition

explanation.surface: Exaggerating one's condition once the job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to exaggerate, to claim more for something than is true.

clue.text: Latter part of day's regular diet, possibly

parts.note: even means regular, uniform

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone's evening meals are part of a steady diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the closing part of the day.

clue.text: Dearie me! The French are to barrack

parts.note: heck is a mild exclamation of dismay like 'dearie me'
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay that the French are going to jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is British for to jeer or shout down a speaker, as a heckler does.
